headline: South Asia: Yemen’s Houthis launch strikes after Saudi coalition’s 'special operation'
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Yemen’s Houthis launch strikes after Saudi coalition’s 'special operation'.
- Western Russia: Eleven injured in Russian attacks on Dnipropetrovsk and Kherson oblasts.
- Persian Gulf Region: Russian strike kills two, wounds 60, in Zelenskyy’s hometown.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Renowned Iraq War Marine under federal investigation.
- Military Times, one day ago: Renowned Iraq War Marine under federal investigation.
Retired Marine Sgt. Maj. Bradley Kasal is under investigation by the Naval Criminal Investigative Service for allegations over his conduct as an instructor for the Junior Reserve Officers' Training Corps.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Takeaways from the historic summit among Trump, Xi, and Putin.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 18 hours ago: Takeaways from the historic summit among Trump, Xi, and Putin.
SHENZHEN, China (AP): The meeting among United States President Donald Trump, China’s Xi Jinping and Russia’s Vladimir Putin on Thursday was the first-ever sit-down for the leaders of the three countries. They started with talk of a shared responsibility for keeping peace as the victors of World War II and as global powers. But post-meeting readouts by the three nations reflected more symbolism than substance.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 18 hours ago: NIGHT OF HORROR - 13-y-o's hand severed in vicious machete attack at home; suspect held.
A St Catherine family is hoping to get answers after the police detained a suspect believed to linked to a brutal machete attack on a 13-year-old boy multiple times inside his New Prospect home in Bog Walk on Thursday night. The teenager sustained multiple wounds to his head and face, his left hand was severed, and the thumb of his right hand was also severed. Doctors reportedly said most of the wounds are defensive in nature.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America - bottom line: ‘Minefield’ returns for nine nights of memory, theater and reflection.
- Buenos Aires Herald, one day ago: ‘Minefield’ returns for nine nights of memory, theater and reflection.
Lola Arias’ production featuring Argentine and British Malvinas War veterans premiered as part of the Herald’s 150th anniversary celebrations La entrada ‘Minefield’ returns for nine nights of memory, theater and reflection se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Eleven injured in Russian attacks on Dnipropetrovsk and Kherson oblasts.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 7 hours ago: Eleven injured in Russian attacks on Dnipropetrovsk and Kherson oblasts.
Russian drone, artillery and air strikes injured 11 people in Dnipropetrovsk and Kherson oblasts on 21 November, with several people taken to hospital.
- The Moscow Times, Ukrainska Pravda, 9 hours ago: From Crimea to Kyiv, Bridges Become Targets in Russia’s War on Ukraine.
Ukraine’s destruction of the Crimean Bridge’s road span and Russia’s strikes on Kyiv’s bridges mark the latest stages of each side’s war strategy.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 8 hours ago: Finland confirms Ukraine attacked ship linked to Russian military.
Finland has confirmed that Ukrainian drones hit the Russian ship Sparta II, which drifted into Finnish waters, and suspects a Russian helicopter violated its airspace.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Ukrainian mid- and long-range strike drones to be produced in UK.
Ukraine and the UK have signed agreements on the production of Ukrainian middle- and deep-strike drones in Britain with UK funding to supply Ukraine's defence forces.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Russian threats ‘less and less hybrid,’ Von der Leyen says after assassination plot in Denmark.
- Politico Europe, The Moscow Times, 12 hours ago: Russian threats ‘less and less hybrid,’ Von der Leyen says after assassination plot in Denmark.
Danish authorities said they thwarted a Russian plan to kill a Ukrainian rapper in September.

AFRICA

- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 7 hours ago: Russian strike kills two, wounds 60, in Zelenskyy’s hometown.
Attack on Kryvyi Rih comes as Russian missiles land in NATO member Poland and US-led peace efforts face uncertainty.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, The Hindu - International, 6 hours ago: Israeli strike hits food aid vehicle in Gaza, killing three.
Three Palestinians were killed in an Israeli air attack on a vehicle carrying food.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 5 hours ago: Deadly attack in Kyiv as Russia launches barrage against Ukraine.
Russia launched more than 400 drones and 110 missiles across Ukraine overnight, killing at least seven in Kyiv.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 2 hours ago: Bahrain says Iranian attack causes fire at industrial facility.
Bahrain reports no injuries, as Iran's IRGC says it targeted US military positions at two bases in al-Riffa and Awali.
Africa - bottom line: Ukraine: Dashcam captures massive explosion on Lviv street.
- Africanews, one hour ago: Ukraine: Dashcam captures massive explosion on Lviv street.
A dashcam captured the moment a Russian projectile struck a building directly ahead of a car in Lviv, forcing the driver to reverse. The attack killed two people and injured at least 10 others.
- Africanews, 11 hours ago: English captain and Bayern Munich star out of action after ankle injury.
Striker Harry Kane vows to be back for ‘business end of season’ after surgery on a ligament in his ankle which he tore during a match on Friday.
- Africanews, 12 hours ago: Strait of Hormuz: Athlete swims through war zone to expose war's environmental toll.
British endurance swimmer Lewis Pugh completed a 15-kilometre swim through the Strait of Hormuz over three days in November 2026, braving explosions and burning tankers nearby. His three-day challenge aimed to expose the environmental damage caused by the war with Iran.

- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one day ago: South Africa: Joburg Residents Could Face R120,000 Fine for Watering the Lawn.

- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one day ago: South Africa: Cachalia Drops Apartheid Truth Bombs As Latest Stats Show '60 Killed Daily in SA'.
[Daily Maverick] South Africa's latest official crime statistics show that over three months, 5,590 people were murdered in the country. Referencing gang killings and violence, Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia reminded Parliamentarians that apartheid's legacy still affected these crimes and that the most affected areas needed development, not just heightened policing.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one day ago: South Africa: Gbvf Policy Promises Must Turn Into Daily Safety for Women - Deputy President.
[SAnews.gov.za] South Africa must move beyond policy promises and awareness campaigns to deliver real protection for the more than one in three women who still face physical or sexual violence in their lifetime.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 2 days ago: South Africa: North-West Mother Pleads for Help After Daughter Loses Both Legs.
[Scrolla] Pauline Mhlongo says she stays on her feet through the night when it rains because their shack leaks. Former ward councillor Andrew Zimba says the family's unfinished three-bedroom house still needs a roof.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Yemen’s Houthis launch strikes after Saudi coalition’s 'special operation'.
- Dawn (Pakistan), South China Morning Post - China, Taipei Times, The Hindu - International, just now: Yemen’s Houthis launch strikes after Saudi coalition’s 'special operation'.
Yemen’s Houthis launched strikes on the Saudi capital Riyadh on Saturday, after vowing reprisals for a “special operation” by the Saudi-led coalition fighting them. Saudi Arabia has been battling a surge in attacks since fighting reignited in neighbouring Yemen’s civil war this summer, where Riyadh backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis. An AFP journalist reported hearing two explosions shortly after authorities issued an alert, later lifted, saying the city was “under a hostile aerial threat”.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 13 hours ago: FM Dar calls for multilateralism, says bloc or unilateral politics will not work.
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar stressed the importance of multilateralism, saying bloc politics and unilateralism would not work. In an interview with Euronews, the foreign minister said Pakistan’s foreign policy was very clear: it was independent. “We believe in multilateralism,” FM Dar said, emphasising that even in the current environment, countries needed to work “double hard” to support it. “Bloc politics or unilateral politics will not work,” he added.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 7 hours ago: Security forces kill 15 terrorists in Balochistan's Mastung district: state media.
Security forces have killed 15 terrorists during two separate operations in Balochistan’s Mastung district, state media reported on Saturday. According to security sources cited by Radio Pakistan, five terrorists were killed in the first operation, while 10 others were eliminated in the second one. Both were conducted against Fitna al Hindustan under ‘Operation Raddul Fitna 3’, which began in August. The state has designated outlawed Balochistan-based groups as Fitna al Hindustan to highlight India’s role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.
- The Hindu - International, ABC News Australia, Ukrainska Pravda, Times of India - Top Stories, Politico Europe, 2 hours ago: Finland detects drone attack on Russian cargo ship in Baltic.
The Finnish Defence Ministry did not specify who was behind the drone strike, but Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said in a message “War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity... Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor”

New vehicles for drone and anti-drone warfare have been spotted at the site where the Zhuhai air show will be held next month, reflecting China’s push to integrate hi-tech platforms on land battlefields as well as its ambitions in the global defence market. Images and videos circulating online show hardware including two unmanned combat vehicles – one equipped with Hongjian missiles – and a new type of anti-drone tactical vehicle at the site in southeastern China where the air show will be held...

Mexico’s military announced on Saturday that it had captured a drug kingpin on the FBI’s list of 10 most wanted fugitives in an operation that left four soldiers and seven suspected gunmen dead. Fausto Isidro Meza, alias “Chapo Isidro,” was captured on Friday night during a special forces raid in the northwestern state of Sinaloa, along with his alleged second-in-command and a financial operator for his criminal organisation. - South China Morning Post - China, 18 hours ago: ID card checks to tackle ticket touting could slow entry to shows: tourism chief.
Hong Kong’s tourism chief has warned that requiring concertgoers to show identity cards matching the names on their tickets to combat scalping could slow entry to venues, saying arrangements would need to be discussed with organisers for each event. Secretary for Culture, Sports and Tourism Rosanna Law Shuk-pui also told a radio programme on Saturday that the city could record around 55 million visitor arrivals this year, 1.2 million more than the government’s earlier forecast of 53.8...
- South China Morning Post - China, 21 hours ago: Japan’s ‘Rabbit Island’ draws tourists with fluffy bunnies and dark wartime past.
Stepping onto an island in western Japan, tourists squeal with joy at the sight of hundreds of fluffy rabbits, but few realise the land was once home to a secret chemical weapons factory for the country’s Imperial Army. India - bottom line: IB officer shot at by driver inside Haridwar office.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 9 hours ago: IB officer shot at by driver inside Haridwar office.
A disturbing shooting took place in Kankhal, Haridwar, where SP CP Nautiyal, an officer with the Intelligence Bureau, was attacked by his hired driver, Vinod Negi, who was quickly apprehended. The officer has been admitted to the hospital and is said to be in stable condition. Investigations are underway to uncover the motive for the shooting, with no prior offenses linked to Negi being reported.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Mexico drug cartel leader's arrest sparks deadly violence in Sinaloa; 11 killed.
A military operation in Guasave led to the arrest of cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as El Chapo Isidro. The operation triggered widespread violence, resulting in the deaths of 11 people, including soldiers and cartel gunmen. Cartel operatives retaliated by setting up roadblocks and burning vehicles across the city. Local businesses suffered damage, and residents sought shelter amid gunfire and military intervention.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 8 hours ago: US lawmaker turns up heat on Musk over Ukraine Starshield disruptions.
US Representative Jim Himes has warned SpaceX about potential funding cuts if it does not clarify its actions regarding Ukraine. The company faced scrutiny over its restrictions on satellite communications that impacted Ukraine's military operations. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reported systematic disruptions affecting military technology amid ongoing conflict. Disagreements over who controls the Starshield system have arisen among government officials and SpaceX.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 9 hours ago: 'Working to curb India’s rise': US report flags China's support to Pak during Op Sindoor.
In May 2025, China's military support for Pakistan intensified India's security dilemmas. This report reveals Beijing's ongoing strategies aimed at stifling India's strategic advancements through both military and economic tactics. With Pakistan receiving advanced weaponry, India's concerns over a dual-threat scenario have been amplified. The evolving military alliance between China and Pakistan poses greater risks for India moving forward, showcasing a troubling shift in regional security dynamics.

As Longreach locals watch the town's main street pivot towards a growing government and legal sector, some researchers say there is opportunity in buildings left empty by the digital sales transition.
